grades.question: How many ordinary turns does each player take in the standard 16-round game, and what happens (including service rotation and ongoing tile benefits) on a courtship round?
grades.expected_answer: Twelve ordinary turns: four seasons, each three ordinary rounds then a courtship. No player turn, rotation, monument reputation or Servants’ Hall use on courtship; only courtship resolves.
grades.actual_answer: Each player takes twelve ordinary turns: the 16 spaces are four seasons of three ordinary rounds plus a courtship. Courtship has no player turns, service rotation, monument income, or Servants’ Hall use.
grades.reader_evidence: Overview: ‘each player takes twelve ordinary turns. Courtship is an event, with no player turns, service rotation, monument income or Servants’ Hall use.’
grades.reason: Twelve ordinary turns and every specified no-turn courtship exclusion correctly stated.

grades.question: State the ordered procedure for hosting an activity, including when round-track events and ongoing effects happen and where used servants, gentry and the tile go at cleanup.
grades.expected_answer: Rotate service; resolve round event then ongoing effects; choose activity; invite exact required gentry; provide service; enjoy favours; optional market buy; clear board. Used servants to Expended Service, played gentry to personal discard, tile upgraded if needed and returned to correct tableau column; last player advances marker.
grades.actual_answer: Hosting order: (1) move servants from Servants’ Quarters to Available Service, then Expended Service to Servants’ Quarters (each advances one space; do not move expended servants twice); (2) resolve the round-track event, then applicable monument and Servants’ Hall effects in either order; (3) choose an activity tile; (4) invite the exact required gentry; (5) provide required service; (6) take favours, all positive before all negative; (7) optionally buy one improvement; (8) clear: all used servants to Expended Service, played gentry to the personal discard pile, and return the activity tile to its tableau column, flipping/upgrading as required. The last player advances the round marker.
grades.reader_evidence: Turn Structure, Hosting an activity steps 1–8: ‘Check round track, then ongoing tiles’; cleanup sends servants to Expended Service, gentry to personal discard, and returns the tile to its tableau column.
grades.reason: Complete hosting order, event/ongoing priority and used-component cleanup destinations stated.

grades.question: When passing, in what order do you recover servants and gentry, resolve events/ongoing effects, take a passing benefit and buy? What benefits are available in this base-only scope, and may you hire through Butler’s Room as a passing benefit?
grades.expected_answer: All servants directly Available; all personal discard gentry to hand; round event then ongoing effects; choose £200 or free market refresh; optional one tile purchase; last player advances marker. Hiring on pass is expansion/optional and excluded here.
grades.actual_answer: Pass order: all servants directly to Available Service; all gentry in your discard to hand; resolve the round-track event, then ongoing tile effects; choose either £200 or a free Market refresh; optionally buy one tile. Any servant used for an ongoing effect is expended at turn end. Butler’s Room hiring is an activity, not a passing benefit, so you cannot hire through it as a pass benefit.
grades.reader_evidence: Passing: ‘all servants directly to Available Service → all gentry in your discard to hand → round-track event, then ongoing tile effects → choose £200 or a free Market refresh → optional one tile purchase’; Butler’s Room hiring is an activity.
grades.reason: Complete passing order, both base benefits and exclusion of hire-on-pass stated.

grades.question: Your reputation is 6.1 after step 2 and you plan a PR6 activity with PR6 guests, but need four Service Help actions that lower your actual reputation to 3.4. Is this legal, which servants can Service Help refresh, and what reputation is used to screen the tile and guests?
grades.expected_answer: Legal if four needed servants are in Servants’ Quarters and costs payable. Service Help costs 3 increments each, Quarters to Available only. Screening reputation fixed after step 2 before step 3 is level 6 for tile and guests all turn; later loss does not invalidate.
grades.actual_answer: Yes. The PR screen is fixed at the end of step 2, before choosing the activity, so reputation level 6.1 is used to check the PR6 tile and guests. The four Service Help actions may then lower actual reputation to 3.4 without invalidating the activity. Each costs three reputation increments and moves one servant from Servants’ Quarters to Available Service; it cannot take a servant directly from Expended Service. The action is legal as described, since special actions may lower actual reputation after screening.
grades.reader_evidence: Reputation screening: ‘fixed at the end of step 2, before Choose Activity’ and special actions later ‘may lower actual reputation below those PRs without invalidating the activity.’ Service Help moves one servant from Servants’ Quarters to Available Service.
grades.reason: Fixed end-step-2 screening and Quarters-only Service Help support legal PR6 plan despite later loss.

grades.question: How must positive and negative favours be ordered? At minimum reputation can you take a negative reputation favour first to avoid the loss, and what is required to play a guest with a money penalty?
grades.expected_answer: All positive before all negative. Cannot take loss first at minimum; ignore only loss beyond minimum after positives. Must pay money penalty; activity income, VP money or Borrow Money can fund it. If unable to fund full payment cannot play guest.
grades.actual_answer: Resolve all positive favours before all negative favours; choose any order within those groups. grades.question: Give all three special action costs, their per-turn limits and the minimum-reputation restriction. Can service help take a servant straight out of Expended Service?

grades.question: How do you hire with the base Butler’s Room activity, may any gentry attend, where do new hires go, and how does upgrading change the recruiting option?

grades.question: How can an underbutler be acquired in the base game, when is it available, and can another player recruit it?

grades.question: How is a tile’s purchase price calculated in the Market and Reserve, what is the minimum price, and can you buy a tile you already own or one above your reputation?

grades.question: When refilling the Market after a purchase, what happens to remaining tiles, a drawn duplicate, a reserve-eligible tile and multiple newly drawn tiles? Does buying just one tile from a duplicate stack cause a refill?
grades.expected_answer: Slide remaining left; stack drawn duplicate on match and draw again; qualifying Service/PR1 drawn tile to Reserve and draw again; sort new tiles by ascending sorting number when filling multiple spaces. One remaining duplicate keeps space occupied so no refill.
grades.actual_answer: When a Market space empties, slide remaining tiles left and draw replacements into the rightmost spaces. Stack a drawn duplicate on its matching Market tile and draw again; duplicates share one space and its price. If a drawn tile qualifies for Reserve, send it straight to Reserve and draw again. When filling multiple spaces, sort only newly drawn tiles by ascending sorting number. Buying one tile from a two-tile duplicate stack leaves the space occupied, so it causes no refill.
grades.reader_evidence: Refill: ‘slide remaining tiles left’; stack duplicates and draw again; Reserve-eligible tiles go straight to Reserve; sort only new tiles. Buying one from a stack leaves an occupied space.
grades.reason: Old tiles slide; duplicates stack; eligible Reserve routing; new-tile sorting and no-refill stack branch resolved.

grades.question: After seasons 1 and 2, which Market tiles move to Reserve, what exception applies, what happens to later draws, and is a full seasonal Market refresh standard here?

grades.question: For an ordinary (nonfinal) courtship, how are Fairchilds returned, theme scores and ties handled, and objectives discarded? Which direction does the first-player marker then pass?
grades.expected_answer: Return both Fairchilds first. Total current theme-category tile VP including negatives; highest draws VP and chooses one Fairchild to hand. Ties all draw VP and no Fairchild. Each discards one objective face down; shuffle together and bottom objective deck. At season setup first player passes anticlockwise.
grades.actual_answer: At each courtship, first return both Fairchilds to Alderley Hall. In courtships 1–3, score the current theme’s tile VP, including negatives; only the face-up hybrid category counts. The highest score wins one VP card and chooses one Fairchild for hand. On a tie for highest, each tied player draws one VP card and no Fairchild is awarded. Every player discards one secret objective; shuffle the discards together and put them face down on the bottom of the objective deck. After the first three courtships, pass the first-player marker anticlockwise (as part of seasonal upkeep).
grades.reader_evidence: Courtship and seasonal upkeep: both Fairchilds return first; current theme score/tie handling, objective discards, and anticlockwise first-player pass are specified.
grades.reason: Fairchild return, current-theme negatives, winner/tie awards, objective destination and anticlockwise marker resolved.

grades.question: How does final courtship differ in scoring and tie resolution, and what last actions are permitted before end-game scoring?
grades.expected_answer: Sum tile VP in all four revealed theme categories, repeated categories count repeatedly/double for two. Highest wins Fairchild+VP; tied highest reputation level breaks tie ignoring wheel position; if still tied no Fairchild, tied winners draw VP. After courtship final special actions and VP-card benefits if possible, then scoring.
grades.actual_answer: Final courtship scores tile VP across all four revealed themes; repeated categories count each time, including negative VP. The highest gets one VP card and a Fairchild. A tie is broken by highest reputation level, ignoring wheel position; if still tied, no Fairchild is awarded and tied winners draw VP cards under the tie rule. Players discard the final objective, then have a final chance to use special actions and VP cards for benefits where possible before scoring. Only a Fairchild won in final courtship retains its 8 VP for final scoring.

grades.question: List all end-game VP categories, the points for reputation levels 1–7, wealth rounding, and the complete victory tiebreak sequence.
grades.expected_answer: Tiles including negative; gentry in hand/discard incl final Fairchild and negatives; remaining objectives; reputation 1,3,6,10,15,21,28 for levels1–7; servants2 each; £200 per1VP rounded down; unused VP cards. Tie: final Fairchild holder, then highest rep level ignoring position, then shared victory.

grades.actual_answer: A housekeeper may substitute for a lady’s maid only when no lady’s maids are available. With a Brushing Room in your tableau, a footman may substitute for a valet only when no valets are available. An underbutler may substitute for any base male servant (butler, valet, footman) even when that servant type remains available.
grades.reader_evidence: Servants and hiring: substitution rules for housekeeper, footman with Brushing Room, and underbutler.
grades.reason: Housekeeper/BrushingRoom availability conditions and underbutler unrestricted base-male substitutions resolved.

grades.question: How can an underbutler be acquired in the base game, when is it available, and can another player recruit it?
grades.expected_answer: Only acquire Butler’s Pantry; gain underbutler from supply immediately into Expended Service. Cannot hire with Butler’s Room or hire-servant VP card; unique, cannot be recruited. He is not immediately available: normally Expended to Quarters at the next service rotation, then Available at the second subsequent rotation. A pass or Refresh Service VP card can make him available sooner; once in Quarters, Service Help or the Quarters tile can allow earlier use.
grades.actual_answer: The only way to acquire an underbutler is to purchase Butler’s Pantry; take one from supply immediately into Expended Service. It is not immediately available: normally it moves to Servants’ Quarters at your next service rotation and to Available Service at your second subsequent rotation. Passing or a Refresh Service VP card can make it available earlier; once it is in Quarters, Service Help or the Servants’ Quarters tile can permit earlier use. Another player cannot recruit it: the upgraded Butler’s Room recruits only common servants, and underbutlers cannot be hired through Butler’s Room or Hire Servant VP cards.
grades.reader_evidence: Butler’s Pantry paragraph gives acquisition, Expended Service destination and rotation timing; Butler’s Room paragraph limits recruiting to common servants; Hire Servant VP cards exclude underbutlers.
grades.reason: Pantry-only acquisition, immediate Expended placement, second-rotation availability/earlier refresh, and unique recruitment immunity resolved.

grades.question: How is a tile’s purchase price calculated in the Market and Reserve, what is the minimum price, and can you buy a tile you already own or one above your reputation?
grades.expected_answer: Market space price plus tile modifier; Reserve £300 plus modifier; minimum £100. Cannot acquire duplicates by any means. May purchase above reputation; PR restricts play only.
grades.actual_answer: Market price is the market-space price plus the tile’s printed price modifier. Reserve price is £300 plus the modifier. A tile cannot cost less than £100. You may not acquire a duplicate tile you already own by any means. Reputation does not restrict purchasing, so a tile above your reputation may be bought.
grades.reader_evidence: Builders’ Market and Reserve: ‘market-space price plus the tile’s printed price modifier’; Reserve base price £300; minimum £100; never acquire a duplicate; reputation does not restrict purchasing.
grades.reason: Both price formulas, floor, duplicate ban and above-reputation acquisition permission resolved.

grades.question: When refilling the Market after a purchase, what happens to remaining tiles, a drawn duplicate, a reserve-eligible tile and multiple newly drawn tiles? Does buying just one tile from a duplicate stack cause a refill?
grades.expected_answer: Slide remaining left; stack drawn duplicate on match and draw again; qualifying Service/PR1 drawn tile to Reserve and draw again; sort new tiles by ascending sorting number when filling multiple spaces. One remaining duplicate keeps space occupied so no refill.
grades.actual_answer: When a Market space becomes empty, slide remaining tiles left and draw replacements into the rightmost spaces. Stack a drawn duplicate on its matching tile already in the Market and draw again. A Reserve-eligible tile goes straight to Reserve, then draw again. If filling multiple spaces, sort only the new tiles by ascending sorting number. Buying one tile from a two-tile stack leaves that space occupied, so it does not trigger a refill.
grades.reader_evidence: Builders’ Market and Reserve → Refill specifies sliding, duplicate stacking, Reserve routing, sorting new tiles, and that buying one from a two-tile stack leaves an occupied space.
grades.reason: Old tiles slide; duplicates stack; eligible Reserve routing; new-tile sorting and no-refill stack branch resolved.

grades.question: After seasons 1 and 2, which Market tiles move to Reserve, what exception applies, what happens to later draws, and is a full seasonal Market refresh standard here?
grades.expected_answer: After season1 all Service except Largest Wine Cellar; after season2 PR1. Later eligible draws go straight Reserve. Full Market refresh after first three courtships standard under compendium/corrigendum; old stable-market aid incomplete.
grades.actual_answer: After courtship 1, move all Market Service tiles except Largest Wine Cellar to Reserve; later Service tiles drawn go directly there, with the same exception. After courtship 2, also move all Market PR1 tiles to Reserve; later PR1 draws go directly there. Largest Wine Cellar never enters Reserve. A full Market refresh after each of the first three courtships is standard in this rules scope.
grades.reader_evidence: Open Reserve: after courtship 1 Service tiles move except Largest Wine Cellar and future Service draws go there; after courtship 2 PR1 tiles move and future PR1 draws go there. Refresh: full refresh after each of the first three courtships; standard scope confirms it is required.
grades.reason: Both Reserve openings, WineCellar exception, future draws and default first-three-season refresh resolved.

grades.question: For an ordinary (nonfinal) courtship, how are Fairchilds returned, theme scores and ties handled, and objectives discarded? Which direction does the first-player marker then pass?
grades.expected_answer: Return both Fairchilds first. Total current theme-category tile VP including negatives; highest draws VP and chooses one Fairchild to hand. Ties all draw VP and no Fairchild. Each discards one objective face down; shuffle together and bottom objective deck. At season setup first player passes anticlockwise.
grades.actual_answer: At each courtship, first return both Fairchilds to Alderley Hall, wherever held. In courtships 1–3, score the current face-up theme’s tile VP, including negative values; only the currently face-up hybrid category counts. The highest scorer draws one VP card and chooses one Fairchild for their hand. If tied for highest, each tied player draws one VP card and no one gets a Fairchild. Every player discards one secret objective; shuffle simultaneous discards together and put them on the bottom of the deck. After courtships 1–3, pass the first-player marker anticlockwise.
grades.reader_evidence: Courtship and seasonal upkeep gives the return order, theme scoring, winner and tie outcomes, objective discard, and seasonal order including passing first-player marker anticlockwise.
grades.reason: Fairchild return, current-theme negatives, winner/tie awards, objective destination and anticlockwise marker resolved.

grades.question: How does final courtship differ in scoring and tie resolution, and what last actions are permitted before end-game scoring?
grades.expected_answer: Sum tile VP in all four revealed theme categories, repeated categories count repeatedly/double for two. Highest wins Fairchild+VP; tied highest reputation level breaks tie ignoring wheel position; if still tied no Fairchild, tied winners draw VP. After courtship final special actions and VP-card benefits if possible, then scoring.
grades.actual_answer: At final courtship, return Fairchilds as usual and score tile VP for all four revealed theme cards; repeated categories count each time, including negative VP. Highest score gets one VP card and a Fairchild. On a tie, highest reputation level breaks it, with wheel position ignored; if still tied, no Fairchild is awarded and tied winners draw VP cards under the courtship tie rule. Discard the final objective. Then players may take a final chance to use special actions and VP cards for their benefits where possible before the marker moves to Wedding Bells and scoring.
grades.reader_evidence: Final courtship paragraph specifies all-four-theme scoring, ties, final objective discard, and final opportunity to use special actions and VP cards.
grades.reason: All-four-theme/repeated-category score, level tiebreak, persistent tie and last actions resolved.

grades.question: List all end-game VP categories, the points for reputation levels 1–7, wealth rounding, and the complete victory tiebreak sequence.
grades.expected_answer: Tiles including negative; gentry in hand/discard incl final Fairchild and negatives; remaining objectives; reputation 1,3,6,10,15,21,28 for levels1–7; servants2 each; £200 per1VP rounded down; unused VP cards. Tie: final Fairchild holder, then highest rep level ignoring position, then shared victory.
grades.actual_answer: End-game VP categories are improvement tiles (printed face-up VP, including negatives), gentry in hand and discard (including negatives, family, and final Fairchild; dismissed guests excluded), fulfilled objectives, reputation, servants, wealth, and retained unused VP cards. Reputation levels 1–7 score respectively 1, 3, 6, 10, 15, 21, and 28 VP. Wealth scores 1 VP per £200, rounded down. Victory ties go first to the tied player with the final Fairchild; otherwise the tied player with the highest reputation level wins; if still tied, victory is shared. Reputation wheel position does not break the tie.
grades.reader_evidence: Final VP table lists each source, the reputation sequence and £200 rounded-down wealth scoring; victory paragraph gives Fairchild, reputation-level, then shared-victory tiebreaks.
grades.reason: Every requested VP source, reputation-level schedule, wealth rounding and complete tiebreak sequence resolved.

grades.question: How many objectives do you normally receive and retain for scoring in a standard game, what happens to simultaneous discards, and must tile objectives show upgraded tiles?
grades.expected_answer: 5 setup+2 Draw Objectives=7; discard1 each of4 courtships leaves3. Shuffle simultaneous face-down discards before bottom deck. Extra objective effects increase final total by1 each. Tile objectives require possession at end, no upgrade required.
grades.actual_answer: Normally each player gets five secret objectives at setup and draws two more on round 6. Discard one at each of the four courtships, leaving three to score. Shuffle simultaneous discards together, then put them face down on the bottom of the objective deck. A tile objective requires owning the named tile at game end; it does not need to be upgraded.
grades.reader_evidence: Objectives and VP cards: five at setup plus two on round 6; discard one at each of four courtships, leaving three; simultaneous discards are shuffled together; tile objectives require owning tiles, not upgrading them.
grades.reason: Five plus two minus four leaves three; simultaneous discards shuffled/bottomed; upgrade not required.

grades.question: When can VP cards be used for benefits, where do used cards go, and what happens to retained cards at game end?
grades.expected_answer: Immediately on draw or anytime own turn; final chance after final courtship. Reveal and discard to bottom VP deck for benefit; may use several. Retain hidden with objectives and score printed VP if not discarded; no both benefit and VP.
grades.actual_answer: A VP card’s benefit may be used immediately when drawn, at any time on your later turn (multiple cards may be used), and once more after final courtship before scoring. Used VP cards go to the bottom of the VP deck. Retained, unused cards stay hidden with objectives and score their printed VP at game end; a card cannot provide both its benefit and final VP.
grades.reader_evidence: VP card rules state when benefits can be used, that used cards go to the bottom of the VP deck, and retained cards stay hidden with objectives; you cannot take both benefit and final VP.
grades.reason: All VP-card use windows, bottom-deck destination, retained scoring and benefit/VP exclusivity resolved.

grades.question: Explain the mandatory flip rules for a normal activity tile, an already-upgraded tile, a hybrid, and a tile that upgrades into an ongoing monument. Which category counts for a hybrid at courtship and for objectives?
grades.expected_answer: First use normal tile flips to upgrade at cleanup, mandatory; upgraded stays. Hybrid flips each use and moves correct category, starts underlined hybrid icon side. Activity-to-monument flips after first use and never hosts again. Only currently face-up hybrid category counts.
grades.actual_answer: A normal activity tile must flip to its rose/upgrade side after its first use; once upgraded, it stays on that side on later uses. A hybrid starts with its underlined icon showing, flips after every use, and moves to the newly face-up category. A tile that upgrades into an ongoing monument (Queen’s Suite or Lionheart Suite) has one activity use, then becomes a monument and can never host again; its monument benefit starts on subsequent turns. For a hybrid, only its currently face-up category counts at courtship and for objectives.
grades.reader_evidence: Improvements and ongoing effects gives normal and hybrid flip rules and says only the face-up category counts for courtship and objectives; Monuments and suite entries describe suite upgrade into monument and later benefit.
grades.reason: Mandatory normal flip, already-upgraded persistence, hybrid alternation/category and one-use monument conversion resolved.

grades.question: When do monuments and Servants’ Hall work on a hosting turn and a pass turn? How does Servants’ Hall use a servant, and may it target a player at minimum reputation?
grades.expected_answer: After event in step2 hosting or step3 pass. Monuments1rep per ordinary turn, no courtship. Hall any one available servant on tile to lower opponent1 gain1; used servant expended end turn; still host activity/pass. Cannot target minimum-rep opponent.
grades.actual_answer: Monuments resolve during the ongoing-effects step on ordinary turns, whether hosting or passing; each gives one reputation. There is no monument income during courtship. Servants’ Hall also resolves during the ongoing-effects step (step 2 when hosting, step 3 when passing): place one available servant on it to reduce one opponent’s reputation by one and gain one reputation yourself. That servant cannot also staff the activity and goes to Expended Service at turn end. You may not target a player at minimum reputation.
grades.reader_evidence: Monuments: one reputation per ordinary turn during ongoing effects, hosting or passing, no courtship income. Servants’ Hall specifies its timing, one available servant, reputation changes, expending, and minimum-reputation targeting restriction.
grades.reason: Hosting/pass ongoing timing, Hall servant use/destination, normal monument income and minimum-target immunity resolved.

grades.question: Compare Heritage Guest Suite, Queen’s Suite and Lionheart Suite: which guest is used, service and doubling rules, subsequent tile state, and whether their single-guest count can be changed.
grades.expected_answer: Heritage one casual from hand, footman tile and guest normal service; double all favours including negative, stays upgraded activity. Queen one prestige from hand, housekeeper tile and normal guest service; double1 chosen favour others normal; upgrades monument. Lionheart butler tile draws1 prestige from deck no guest service, double all nonnegative favours, keep guest to discard; upgrades monument. All fixed1 cannot modify count.
grades.actual_answer: Heritage Guest Suite uses one casual guest from hand and a footman on the tile; provide the guest’s normal service. It doubles all guest favours, including negative ones, then upgrades and remains an activity tile. Queen’s Suite uses one prestige guest from hand and a housekeeper on the tile; provide normal guest service. It doubles one chosen favour and resolves the others normally, then upgrades into a monument. Lionheart Suite draws one prestige guest from the deck to attend, uses a butler on the tile, and requires no personal guest service. It doubles nonnegative favours while negative favours are excluded from doubling; keep the drawn guest and put it in your discard at cleanup, then the tile upgrades into a monument. Each suite has a fixed count of one guest that cannot be increased or decreased.
grades.reader_evidence: Suite activity table lists each guest source/type, tile service, guest service, favour doubling, cleanup and later tile state; following paragraph says all three have a fixed count of one guest.
grades.reason: All three suites’ guest origins, tile/guest service, distinct doubling, later state and fixed-one count resolved.
